name: Apideck
description: One API so a software company can ship accounting connections to QuickBooks, Xero, NetSuite, and others without building each one. It also covers CRM, HR, shops, and file storage. Antwerp.

mentions.evidence: In a March 2023 interview the CEO said about $600,000 a year, 100 percent growth year over year, 75 customers, an average contract around $10,000, cash flow of negative $360,000, and 10 employees, 9 of them engineers. The 2022 figure was $300,000 a year. He said a $1 million SAFE in June 2022 at a $13 million valuation. GetLatka estimates about $1.3 million as of October 2024, with 13 employees. The homepage, read 11 November 2026, shows more than 50 accounting integrations. The 2023 interview, the 2022 figure, and the 2024 estimate are three readings.
mentions.indieAngle: One stubborn ledger that the broad APIs do not cover. Go deep on that one, the way Conductor did with QuickBooks Desktop.

whyItPrints: A vertical product eventually has to sync the customer's books. This sells that plumbing. Contracts were about $10,000.
whyThisMatters: A product that serves one trade eventually has to push the customer's books. Building QuickBooks, then Xero, then NetSuite, one by one, is a long job. Apideck sells that plumbing as one API, plus CRM, HR, shops, and file storage. Antwerp. In a March 2023 interview the CEO said about 600,000 dollars a year, growing 100 percent, with 75 customers and an average contract around 10,000 dollars. Cash flow was negative 360,000 dollars. Ten people, nine of them engineers. He said 2022 was 300,000 dollars, and a 1 million dollar SAFE in June 2022 at a 13 million dollar valuation. GetLatka estimates about 1.3 million as of October 2024, with 13 employees. On 11 November 2026 the homepage was showing more than 50 accounting integrations. The interview, the 2022 line, and the later estimate are three readings, not one total. The figure is self-reported, which means the founder said it, or a data site estimated it. I did not open the books.
